verdict: REVISE, matching the pre-registered threshold literally. Round 1 (cheapest falsifier) PASSED: a generative provider reflection-forwards into a real Myriad-CLI-produced, checker.Compile-built satellite DLL via Expr.Call(realMethodInfo, args), requiring sourceAssemblies=Assembly.LoadFrom-at-construction (four attempts to find; Assembly.Load(bytes) and RegisterGeneratedTargetAssembly both fail with distinct errors). Round 2 (regeneration + live pickup) FAILED: Assembly.LoadFrom's required file-lock (needed for the same source/target identity match Round 1 depends on) blocks the separate SatelliteBuilder process from overwriting Satellite.dll ('Could not open file for writing'), so the FileSystemWatcher-driven Invalidate() never fires. Review (03-review.md) could not independently rebuild/rerun due to a sustained command-safety-classifier outage on effectful commands during its entire window (read-only tooling worked; every dotnet build/run was refused) -- this is a real, disclosed gap against the pre-registered requirement that Movement 4 independently reproduce at a different parameter, not a silent gap. What the review did instead: verified the saved run-logs are byte-identical to the checked-in source (diffed against the surviving scratch build), verified every cited SDK line reference resolves in the vendored ProvidedTypes.fs/.fsi, and independently confirmed from src/Myriad.Sdk/build/Myriad.Sdk.targets that Myriad's real generation is a short-lived per-input <Exec> that never holds a lock across edits (supporting 02-results' realism framing). Four objections sharpen the verdict beyond 02-results: (1) the provider is hand-fit to create/name/age/email and cannot generalize without new code; the one materially different shape already sitting in Generated.fs (map, two FSharpFunc-typed params) was never tried, and whether Expr.Call forwards function-typed args through the SDK's source-to-target conversion is the single most important open question, unresolved by this review's own outage; (2) Round 1's 'two independent checks agree' is weaker than it sounds because name/age are trivial identity echoes indistinguishable from a reimplementation -- the forwarding claim rests on the Expr.Call source fact, not on runtime values, a NULL-adjacent trap Q001 already named; (3) Round 2's failure lands on the type provider's only differentiator over an ordinary ProjectReference for this cross-project case (live re-exposure via Invalidate()+FileSystemWatcher) -- BACKLOG item 15's own text concedes this is the TP's sole reason to exist here, and both realism branches (long-lived IDE host vs. short-lived per-build process) remove that reason, which the review says should lead any summary of this quartet, not trail it; (4) the REVISE threshold's own named workaround (Assembly.Load(bytes) per Q011) is ruled out by this quartet's own attempts 1 and 3, so the repair path REVISE normally presumes is unproven -- only an untested collectible-AssemblyLoadContext alternative remains, which 02-results itself flags may just relocate the tension. KILL and NULL were both explicitly considered and ruled out: the sourceAssemblies mechanism was not rejected by IL emission (the design's headline KILL risk), and exposing/forwarding a real external type+value is materially more than Q008/Q09/Q11's synthetic markers. Top follow-up, prioritized by the review: rerun Round 1 on the map shape to settle generalization; only then is the collectible-ALC Round 2 mitigation worth attempting.
